rs-bs-walk-hop.back: Walk: one print ahead of the next. Many songbirds hop in pairs.

rs-bs-winter-toes.front: Why do grouse tracks look wider in winter?
rs-bs-winter-toes.back: Grouse grow comb like fringes on their toes for snow.

rs-bs-snow-roost.front: Hole in soft snow with droppings inside and wing marks beside?
rs-bs-snow-roost.back: A grouse snow roost. It dove in and burst out.

rs-bs-moult.front: One or two feathers on a trail?
rs-bs-moult.back: Often moult or preening. A pile means something died.

rs-bs-goose-field.back: Geese fed there recently. Geese drop about 6 times an hour while feeding.

rs-bs-goose-scout.front: When do you scout a goose field?
rs-bs-goose-scout.back: Late in the afternoon, then set up there next morning (with consent).

rs-bs-puff.front: Puff of feathers after your shot?
rs-bs-puff.back: A hit. Mark the fall on a tree or rock and walk straight to it.

rs-bs-s42.front: Migratory Birds Regulations s. 42: wounded bird?
rs-bs-s42.back: You must ensure it is killed and retrieved as soon as the circumstances permit, and have means to retrieve.

rs-bs-quail-feed.back: Scratched soil and leaf litter patches under shrubs near cover.
